match.reason: No point in the bank covers the marketing mix; the closest, market research for a new business, is about learning what customers want, not about combining product, price, promotion and place.

draft.title: The marketing mix
card: The marketing mix is the set of choices a business makes to meet the needs of its target market. The choices are called the 4Ps, and they work best when they fit together.
what is sold, including its features and quality. Price is the amount the customer pays.
how the business tells customers about the product and persuades them to buy. Place is how and where customers can get it.

A business selling a service adds three more Ps: people (the staff who deliver it), processes (the steps the customer goes through) and physical evidence (things the customer can see, such as the premises or uniforms).
draft.remember: The marketing mix is the 4Ps chosen together for one target market, and services add three more Ps.

a.q: Which choice is part of a business's place decision?
opts: Selling through its own website and in stores
Running a social media campaign for the product
Setting the amount customers pay for the product
Choosing the quality of materials in the product
a.why: Place is about how and where customers can get the product, so selling through a website and stores is a place choice. A social media campaign is promotion, because it tells customers about the product and persuades them to buy.
a.clue: Place is about how customers get the product.

b.q: Priya runs a dental clinic in Parramatta. She trains her receptionists to greet patients warmly. Which part of the mix is this?
opts: People
Promotion
Processes
Physical evidence
b.why: Receptionists are staff who deliver the service to patients, so this is people. It is not processes, which are the steps a patient goes through, such as booking and payment. It is not promotion, because the training is about delivering the service, not advertising it.
b.clue: Think about who delivers the service, not the steps.

a.best: Selling through its own website and in stores

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about who delivers the service, not the steps' points straight at 'people' (the card's wording for staff who deliver it) and rules out processes, so it gives the answer away.
